Hawaii.max_claim: $5,000 (no limit for residential security deposit cases)
Hawaii.waiting_period: 1 year after discharge for deferred pleas; varies by offense
Hawaii.what_qualifies: arrests not charged or dismissed, acquittals, deferred pleas; some convictions under 2024 Clean Slate law

Idaho.what_qualifies: arrests not charged, acquittals, dismissed cases (not convictions)

Illinois.filing_fee: about $89–$264 depending on county and claim size
Illinois.waiting_period: none for acquittals/dismissals; 2–3 years for sealing; 5 years for certain probation
Illinois.what_qualifies: dismissed/acquitted cases can be expunged; most convictions can be sealed

Indiana.waiting_period: 1 year for arrests; 5 years for misdemeanors; 8–10 years for felonies
Indiana.what_qualifies: most arrests, misdemeanors, and many felonies (not sex or violent offenses)

Iowa.waiting_period: 180 days for acquittals/dismissals; 8 years for misdemeanor convictions
Iowa.what_qualifies: acquittals and dismissed charges; some misdemeanor convictions

Kansas.lawyer_allowed: generally no — only if the other side is represented
Kansas.waiting_period: 3 years for misdemeanors/minor felonies; 5 years for serious felonies and DUI
Kansas.what_qualifies: most misdemeanors, minor felonies, dismissed charges, diversions (not violent or sex offenses)

Kentucky.filing_fee: about $35–$75 depending on how the defendant is served
Kentucky.what_qualifies: misdemeanors, violations, and many Class D felonies; acquittals and dismissals

Louisiana.filing_fee: about $100–$160 depending on parish and court
Louisiana.waiting_period: 5 years for misdemeanors, 10 years for felonies, after sentence completion
Louisiana.what_qualifies: most misdemeanors and non-violent felonies (not sex crimes or crimes of violence)

Maine.waiting_period: 4 years after sentence for eligible youthful offenses
Maine.what_qualifies: sealing for low-level Class E misdemeanors committed at ages 18–21

Maryland.waiting_period: none for acquittals/dismissals; 3 years for probation-before-judgment; 3–5 years for most convictions
Maryland.what_qualifies: acquittals/dismissals, probation-before-judgment, stet, pardons, and many misdemeanor and felony convictions
